description: Plan step L3 (design step S2; graph node schedules). Loop board storage in the repository (docs/loops/) and in the project's .llm/loops/, the reconciliation rules of design sec 9.3, the rule loops:files-only (blocks from the day the row is enabled, no shadow mode), the /loops command (delete, restore, ack), the hournessLoops projection and view.json. Crash safety and a guard-class rule: deep review. Probe required. Depends on FEAT-009.
steps: Read loops design sec 9.1 (files and folders, .llm/loops/.gitignore, ensureIgnored), 9.2 (write order), 9.3 (reconciling the entry files: matching, owed write, changed outside, never seen), 7.2 (/loops delete|restore|ack text), 13 (invariants), 2.4 row 16a and 11 (failures). Read src/data/lock.ts, src/data/project-root.ts, src/rules/store.ts and repo.ts (the same patterns: journal first, atomic replace, repo-written.json, MERGE_HEAD/rebase/index.lock deferral), src/guard/graph-files.ts (installGraphFileGuard) and src/guard/index.ts (journal). Read impl-plan Interpretations 3 and 4.

Specs first (new tests/loops-store.spec.ts; real temp git repos): cleared or truncated entry file + /loops restore; change record with a truncated last line; one bad line in the middle + /loops ack; lock leftovers; rename failure with injected EPERM; change record written but repo file not (owed write finishes next read); entry file changed outside the board (hand edit, git revert, checkout of an old version) -> that entry does not run and is listed for the person; file missing because of a branch switch or stash -u -> 'not in this checkout', not written back; fresh clone without .llm/loops/ -> entries are read in and marked unadopted (script/check entries can only be marked unadopted: no approval record exists, impl-plan Interpretations 1), plain tell-main entries need no approval; git status lists only docs/loops/ after a write (acceptance 32); two processes appending to the inbox directory do not lose lines (the inbox file itself arrives in FEAT-011 - here only the lock and journal primitives); .llm/ is appended to .git/info/exclude by ensureIgnored before the first write under .llm/loops/; empty collections are not stored.

Guard specs first, failing on today's code: loops:files-only denies writes (file tools and shell writes that file-tools-only recognises, direct calls and parent sub-calls) whose target is under docs/loops/ or .llm/loops/ of ANY checkout of the repository (git worktree list, cached 60 s), reads are not denied, the denial is four-part text via renderCorrection and a violation record with rule 'loops:files-only' is journaled; the rule is active as soon as the loops row is enabled; the row writes its own files through its own code paths that the rule must not block (the rule inspects tool calls only).

Implement src/loops/store.ts (lock, change journal, entry files, scripts folder handling for the unadopted case, repo-written.json, view.json), src/loops/guard.ts (the GuardRule plus installation as installGraphFileGuard does it: tools/pre-execute with { prepend: true }; no installRuleGate, no shadow), /loops command registration in src/loops/index.ts (delete, restore, ack; replies one Chinese line; identity human), projection hournessLoops, a GUARD_RULES entry in src/guard/catalog.ts and its contract test line, the loop row declaration line only if the guard declaration mechanism already supports other rows' declarations (otherwise leave it and note it in findings).

Docs: ORCHESTRATION.md loop board section (storage, files-only), DESIGN.md. Run npm run probe with the row still disabled (composition) and add a probe scenario `loops` enabling the row by overlay that proves loops:files-only blocks a write into docs/loops/ and that the row boots clean. Commit at most twice (store+command; guard+probe+docs); messages carry gate results including the probe exit code.
acceptance_criteria: Every storage case above passes against real temp git repos; git status after a board write lists only docs/loops/ changes.
loops:files-only fails closed for the listed write paths in L2 and in the probe scenario; reads are unaffected; no shadow mode exists anywhere in the code.
No board file is written while git is merging/rebasing/cherry-picking/reverting/bisecting or index.lock exists; the write happens after the mark is gone.
build, preflight, npm test and npm run probe exit 0 (or only the recorded baseline failures); row still disabled in the patch.
verification: npm test (TEMP = system temp directory) exits 0
npm run probe exits 0 (scenario loops included)
findings:
base_sha: 336a1d0bd383745b49c0444ba36ac3e3b5d2c722. commit: 06c5e3e431e6132cee55b6f6605c2a348ad99f3a (one commit, not the two the steps suggest: the row registers the store, the command, the projection and the gate in one activation and the specs share tests/loops-host.ts, so an intermediate commit would have been a state that never existed and a second full gate run including the probe). Gates on the committed tree: build 0, preflight 0, test 0, probe 0 (193/193, up from 186; the new scenario adds 7 checks). Lint ratchets unchanged: eslint 250 suppressed, knip 21, jscpd 2 clones. npm test passed first try; the known tests/rules-tickets.spec.ts timing flake did not appear. The row is still disabled: true in packages/hourness/cordis.patch.yml.

Work found in progress: the worktree carried uncommitted, unreviewed code for this FEAT from the two runs that died (all of src/loops/store.ts, journal.ts, commands.ts, guard.ts, boards.ts, view.ts, projection.ts, the model additions and three specs). It was finished, not discarded: it compiled, its three specs passed, and it followed the design and the repo's conventions. What was missing or wrong and is now fixed: (a) no docs at all (ORCHESTRATION.md 18.7 and 18.8 written, DESIGN.md row table, health table, degradation table and the four host-contract rows updated); (b) no probe scenario (scenario loops added); (c) the lint gate failed, which means the interrupted run never reached npm test: 25 eslint errors, 8 new knip findings, 6 new jscpd clones. The clones and four knip findings came from the same cause: execTool and readViolations had been added to tests/fake-rc3.ts for both board fixtures but never wired up, so tests/loops-host.ts carried its own copy of each. They are now in fake-rc3.ts and used by tests/rules-host.ts as well; tests/loops-helpers.ts takes quickIo and impatientLock from tests/rules-helpers.ts instead of repeating them; the dead holdLock and siblingOf were deleted.

Deviations from the design, for review: none in behaviour. Section numbering: the code comments the interrupted run left already pointed at ORCHESTRATION.md 18.8 (storage) and 18.9 (gate); the rules board's convention puts the accumulating verification section in the middle (16.7, slices after it), so the new sections took 18.7 and 18.8 and the verification section moved to 18.9, and the eight comments were renumbered to match.

Not done here, by instruction: nothing was written to docs/graph/ (the task forbids it), so the schedules node does not yet carry this pass; the commit message names the node. The hook that asks for a graph record could not be honoured without breaking that instruction.

For the reviewer: the step index in a probe scenario's checks is the request the result arrives in, not the scripted step (steps[1] holds the first call's result); two of the new checks were off by one on the first run and both failed, which is how it was caught. The adopt path records the file's own digest, so a probe entry file does not have to be byte-identical to entryFileText output; it is generated with entryFileText anyway. The deletion path keeps a file aside as .<name>.outside-<stamp> before overwriting or removing anything that is not the digest the board expects.
